title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings and word problems. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation behind the item, used only by the test that checks the answer key.
directions: Show your work. When a question asks for simplest form, simplify all the way.

items.prompt: Write a fraction equal to {3/5} with a denominator of 20.
What number goes in the box?  {4/7} = 12/☐
Are {6/9} and {10/15} equal? Show how you know.
A pizza is cut into 8 slices and Ana eats 6 of them. What fraction of the pizza did she eat? Write it in simplest form.
A recipe needs {2/3} cup of milk. Your measuring cup is marked in twelfths. How many twelfths of a cup do you need?
Write a fraction equal to {2/9} with a denominator of 36.
What number goes in the box?  {5/6} = {?/30}
Are {4/10} and {6/15} equal? Show how you know.
A class has 30 students and 12 of them walk to school. What fraction of the class walks? Write it in simplest form.
A board is marked in sixteenths of an inch. Where is the {3/4} inch mark? Write it in sixteenths.
